paragraphs.source_en: For 90 per cent of the planet's history there has been no fire on Earth. While there were volcanic eruptions, there was not enough oxygen in the atmosphere to sustain combustion. † Thus the rise in oxygen not only allowed more complex life to evolve on Earth, but it gave humanity fire as a tool. We first used it for keeping the night's cold and predators at bay, cooking food, and clearing land. Humanity then learned how to exploit the transformative heat of fire: to bake clay into hard ceramic pottery or building bricks, to make glass, or to smelt metals for tools. Today, we use fire for generating electricity and driving a huge range of industrial processes; and we harness tiny bursts of flame in the engine cylinders of our cars.
